semantic_votes.rationale: The absolute separates closed-schema Core policy from executable prompt instructions, preventing unvalidated JSON text from overriding the dispatch contract.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: The targeted execution-level reference is loaded only while computing or validating execution level, and its JSON is generated from the authoritative Core execution_level_contract.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Retain the data-versus-instruction boundary and the existing closed-schema parser and exact-projection validation.

semantic_votes.rationale: All seven controls are intentionally non-bypassable across execution levels; omitting one can defeat authority, review, validation, or current completion evidence.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: The Core execution_level_contract enumerates exactly seven non_bypassable controls, and even L1 explicitly retains all non-bypassable controls before routed work proceeds.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Keep the exact Core-derived count and fail closed whenever the reference schema or identifier set is invalid.

semantic_votes.rationale: The single complete path is an identity-scoped loop guard, while the adjacent gap-or-transition clause permits justified additional validation paths.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: The authoritative validation_loop fixes complete_path_limit at one for the same validation identity and requires a bound gap or verifiable state transition for another path.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Retain the immediate exception condition and block same-identity repetition lacking a canonical gap or evidence transition.

semantic_votes.rationale: For supplied-artifact review, a no-edit exporter preserves the reviewed workspace boundary; creating a workspace file would mutate and contaminate that diff scope.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: This rule applies only when supplied-artifact mode lacks an actual diff; the utility capsule requires diff-export/no-edit and permits supplied content or a host-native artifact.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Preserve pre/post workspace change-set checks and invalidate the utility result if any workspace change occurs.

semantic_votes.rationale: Declaring formal readiness changes the evidence claim, so ordinary authoring validation cannot substantiate it without the separately required formal evidence gates.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: The Core contract names formal evidence as non-bypassable when formal readiness is declared and separately defines this condition as the validation loop formal_scope_rule.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Keep formal readiness fail closed until the repository's formal-release evidence commands succeed on the final tree.

limitations: This independent ballot is static source-contract review; it does not prove real-host startup, runtime routing behavior, production enforcement, or installed user experience.
The review covers only the packet-named five targets and their current source and authority context; it does not satisfy readability or professional-completeness formal attestations.
